Store listing › Description.body:
Know the moment your build breaks, without keeping a GitHub tab open. GitHub Actions Monitor turns its toolbar icon into a live status light for all the repositories you care about.

AT A GLANCE
• Green: everything passed. Yellow: something is running. Red: something failed (flashing red/green when some passed and some failed). Gray: nothing to show yet.
• Click the icon for each repository's workflows, their state, live run timers, and one-click links to the runs.

EVERY WORKFLOW COUNTS
• The latest run of each workflow decides the status, so a failing CI is never hidden by a deploy that finished after it.
• Cancelled and skipped runs are shown but never raise a false alarm.

FAST WHEN IT MATTERS, QUIET WHEN IT DOESN'T
• Checks every 30 seconds to 5 minutes (your choice), and every 5 seconds while anything is running.
• Rate-limit safe: when nothing changed, GitHub answers "not modified", which does not count against your API limit. The settings page shows live usage.
• Desktop notifications when a workflow starts, succeeds or fails (optional).

MADE FOR REAL PROJECTS
• Watch all branches or a specific branch, and the same repository on several branches.
• Pause and resume repositories you are not working on.
• Autocomplete for your own (including private) and public repositories.
• Light and dark themes. Settings sync across your Chrome devices.

PRIVATE AND READ-ONLY
• One click opens GitHub's token form already set to read-only Actions access, and a built-in check confirms what the token can see.
• It talks only to GitHub's API. No server, no analytics, nothing sent to the developer.
• Your token stays on your device unless you choose to sync it.

More, including setup help: https://levac.net/actions-monitor/

Privacy › Single purpose description.body: Shows the status of GitHub Actions workflow runs for repositories the user chooses: a toolbar icon colored by the combined status, a popup listing each workflow's latest run, and optional notifications when a run starts, succeeds or fails.

Privacy › storage justification.body: Stores the user's settings (the repositories to monitor, the polling interval, the notification preference) in chrome.storage.sync so they follow the user to their other Chrome devices. On the device (chrome.storage.local) it stores the user's GitHub token, the last results shown in the popup, and HTTP ETags that let it re-check repositories with conditional requests. The token is only synced if the user explicitly turns that on.

Privacy › alarms justification.body: Re-checks the monitored repositories' workflow runs on the user's chosen interval (30 seconds to 5 minutes) in the background, so the toolbar icon stays current without the popup being open. Chrome alarms are the Manifest V3 way to run periodic work in a service worker.

Privacy › notifications justification.body: Shows a desktop notification when a monitored workflow starts, succeeds or fails, so the user learns about a broken build without looking at the browser. Notifications can be turned off on the settings page; clicking one opens the workflow run on GitHub.

Privacy › Host permission justification.body: https://api.github.com/*: reads workflow runs (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs), branches and the list of repositories the user can access, through GitHub's official REST API, using the user's own token. It is used to show workflow status and to autocomplete repository names. It only reads; no other hosts are contacted.

Test instructions › Test instructions.body:
Needs a GitHub account (any free account works) and a repository with GitHub Actions; any public repository with Actions can be monitored, e.g. "actions/checkout".

1. Click the toolbar icon, then the gear (or right-click the icon → Options) to open the settings page.
2. Click "Create a read-only token on GitHub". GitHub's fine-grained token form opens with the name and Actions: Read-only already set. Click "Generate token", copy it, paste it into the settings page and click "Save Token". The token check confirms the account and access.
3. Click the toolbar icon, type a repository (e.g. actions/checkout), choose "All branches", click "Add Repo", then "Refresh Now".
4. The toolbar icon and the repository's status dot turn green, yellow or red; the popup lists each workflow with its state and timing. Clicking a workflow opens its run on GitHub.

Store listing › Description.body:
Know the moment your build breaks, without keeping a GitHub tab open. GitHub Actions Monitor turns its toolbar icon into a live status light for all the repositories you care about.

AT A GLANCE
• Green: everything passed. Yellow: something is running. Red: something failed (flashing red/green when some passed and some failed). Gray: nothing to show yet.
• A number on the icon counts failing repositories (or running ones when nothing fails).
• Click the icon for a compact card per repository: its state, and where a failure happened ("Test › npm test"), one click from the log.
• Counts of failing, running and passing repositories above the list; click one to see only those.

EVERY WORKFLOW COUNTS
• The latest run of each workflow decides the status, so a failing CI is never hidden by a deploy that finished after it.
• Cancelled and skipped runs are shown but never raise a false alarm.
• Each workflow's last ten runs at a glance, with the commit, pull request and author behind the latest one.
• Switch off noisy workflows: they stay listed but never turn a repository red.
• Runs waiting for a deployment review or an approval are marked, with a link to review them.

FAST WHEN IT MATTERS, QUIET WHEN IT DOESN'T
• Checks every 30 seconds to 5 minutes (your choice), and every 5 seconds while anything is running.
• Rate-limit safe: when nothing changed, GitHub answers "not modified", which does not count against your API limit. The settings page shows live usage.
• Desktop notifications when a workflow starts, succeeds or fails (optional).

MADE FOR REAL PROJECTS
• Watch all branches or a specific branch, and the same repository on several branches.
• Pause and resume repositories you are not working on.
• Drag repositories into your own order, or sort by name, recent activity or status.
• Pick an owner, then choose from all of its repositories (private ones included). Owners you use are remembered.
• On a repository's GitHub page, the popup offers to add it.
• Light and dark themes. Settings sync across your Chrome devices.

PRIVATE, AND READ-ONLY BY DEFAULT
• One click opens GitHub's token form already set to read-only Actions access, and a built-in check confirms what the token can see.
• Want to re-run failed jobs or cancel a run from the popup? Switch it on in Settings (it then needs a token with Actions write access). Off by default.
• It talks only to GitHub's API. No server, no analytics, nothing sent to the developer.
• Your token stays on your device unless you choose to sync it.

More, including setup help: https://levac.net/actions-monitor/
